holidays.name: Frog Jumping Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate amphibian athletics, inspired by Mark Twain's famous short story about a gambling man and his talented jumping frog. Fans of croaking competition hold hopping contests and sip on pond-themed snacks.
holidays.origin: Inspired by Mark Twain's 1865 story 'The Celebrated Jumping Frog of Calaveras County.' The Calaveras County Fair and Jumping Frog Jubilee in California, held in mid-May, has turned the tale into a real-life tradition.
holidays.funFact: The Calaveras Jubilee world record was set in 1986 by a frog named Rosie the Ribeter, who leapt 21 feet 5.75 inches in three jumps.

holidays.name: National Apple Pie Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to the flaky, cinnamon-scented dessert that has become a symbol of Americana. Bakers and pie lovers celebrate with a warm slice, perhaps with a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top.
holidays.origin: A food holiday of unofficial origin celebrated in the United States, commonly listed on May 13 in food observance calendars. Apple pies themselves date back to medieval England, with recipes appearing as early as the 1300s.
holidays.funFact: The earliest known English apple pie recipe, from around 1381, called for good apples, good spices, figs, raisins, pears, and saffron, but no sugar. Early crusts were called 'coffins' and were often not eaten.

holidays.name: International Hummus Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of the creamy chickpea dip that has conquered snack tables worldwide. Fans dip pita, carrots, and anything else they can get their hands on into this Middle Eastern staple.
holidays.origin: Established in the 2010s by hummus enthusiasts and food promoters, the day grew through social media and food brands. Hummus has been enjoyed across the Middle East for centuries, and the word itself is Arabic for chickpeas.
holidays.funFact: In 2010, a group in Lebanon made the world's largest plate of hummus, weighing over 10 tons, to reclaim the record from Israel in a friendly but fierce Middle Eastern hummus rivalry.

holidays.name: Leprechaun Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the mischievous, gold-hoarding fairies of Irish folklore. People wear green, hunt for rainbows, and keep an eye out for tiny cobblers guarding their pots of gold.
holidays.origin: Leprechaun Day is celebrated on May 13 in the United States as a lighthearted extension of Irish folklore traditions. Leprechauns appear in Irish tales going back to medieval times, where they were solitary shoemakers who could grant wishes if caught.
holidays.funFact: In Ireland, the Carlingford Leprechaun Hunt in County Louth is a real event, and the local area has even protected a patch of land for leprechauns under EU wildlife-style protections.

holidays.name: Fray Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of the iconic Joss Whedon vampire slayer saga to celebrate the comic series Fray, set in a far-future New York where a new Slayer emerges. Fans reread the series and trade geeky banter.
holidays.origin: Fray Day is a fan-driven observance connected to Buffy the Vampire Slayer and its expanded universe. The Fray comic was published by Dark Horse Comics in 2001-2003, featuring a Slayer in the 23rd century.
holidays.funFact: Fray was written by Joss Whedon himself and illustrated by Karl Moline, and it was one of Whedon's first big comic book projects before he helmed Marvel's The Avengers.
